ORG-01.prompt: You are facing a larger undertaking. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I first work out concrete steps before I really get going.
alternatives.B: I start right away with a first foothold to build momentum, and sort out the rest along the way.

EXP-01.prompt: Someone suggests a new approach to your team. You immediately feel: ‘I know this, I have been through something like it before’ – but you cannot explain why just yet. How strongly does this first impression influence your assessment?

VOICE-01.prompt: Your team has more or less agreed on a decision, but you notice a possible counterpoint. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I raise the counterpoint right away, before the group closes the topic.
alternatives.B: I hold the point back so as not to slow the momentum because of a single doubt.

AMB-01.prompt: You receive different feedback on a new idea and cannot yet tell which feedback is more relevant. How much unease does this cause you?

EL-01.prompt: You are torn between two paths, both of which could be tried on a small scale. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I first test a small version in practice before I commit.
alternatives.B: I weigh both paths carefully against each other and then decide on one.

EVI-01.prompt: You have three options and one of them immediately appeals to you most. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: Before committing, I deliberately look for counterarguments so I can spot weaknesses early.
alternatives.B: I start with my favorite to make progress and watch for solid reasons against it along the way.

EXP-02.prompt: A concept looks coherent on paper, but your experience from earlier situations makes you hesitate. How strongly does this prior experience influence your judgment of the plan?

ORG-03.prompt: Several important tasks compete for your attention at the same time. Which describes the way you work better?

alternatives.A: I keep several topics moving in parallel so that nothing comes to a complete stop.
alternatives.B: I focus on a few things and accept that others must wait.

AMB-02.prompt: A problem comes up and there are several plausible explanations, but for now no way to find out which one is true. How much unease does this uncertainty cause you?

VOICE-02.prompt: You notice a delicate point that matters for your shared work but could strain the mood. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I wait for a calm moment and gather my thoughts before I bring it up.
alternatives.B: I raise the topic promptly and openly in the team so that it gets settled.

EVI-02.prompt: Your next step rests on an assumption for which there is no evidence yet. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I check the assumption beforehand with data or facts before I commit.
alternatives.B: I go with my own assessment so as not to end up in endless checking, and correct course when new facts appear.

EXP-03.prompt: Two options seem equally good on the facts. For one of them, however, you strongly recognize something from earlier situations. How strongly does this personal experience tip your choice?

AMB-04.prompt: You are analyzing a problem, but every new piece of information only makes the overall picture more confusing and raises further questions. How much unease does this cause you?

ORG-04.prompt: A task takes much longer than expected. Which describes the way you work better?

alternatives.A: I finish the task I started as planned before I rearrange the schedule.
alternatives.B: I adjust my schedule early to the delay before I carry on.

EL-02.prompt: Your team has two plausible approaches and the discussion is not getting anywhere. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I think the open points through properly in the discussion until we have a common line.
alternatives.B: I suggest cutting the discussion short and testing both approaches on a small scale.

EXP-04.prompt: You face a challenge you have experienced in a similar form several times. How strongly do you draw on these experiences to judge what matters this time?

VOICE-03.prompt: A difficult topic was postponed and never picked up again, although something is still open for you. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I give the topic time and bring it up once it becomes clear in everyday work that it matters.
alternatives.B: I put the topic back on the agenda myself to settle it promptly.

EL-05.prompt: A first attempt does not yet give a clear answer. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I deliberately change one thing and start the next practical attempt right away.
alternatives.B: I take a step back and check fundamentally whether our approach fits.

AMB-05.prompt: You have to keep working on a topic although an important question is still open. How much unease does this cause you?

ORG-02.prompt: A task runs over several weeks without fixed interim deadlines from outside. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I work toward the goal in my own rhythm and notice from the work itself whether I am on track.
alternatives.B: I set myself fixed interim goals to check regularly whether I am still on schedule.

EVI-03.prompt: You have made a decision. Shortly afterwards new information appears that speaks against your decision. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I reopen the decision right away and check whether I should change course.
alternatives.B: I stay with the decision at first and check whether the new information is weighty enough to change course.

EL-04.prompt: You are unsure how others will react to a new idea or offer. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I first work the concept out coherently in peace before I share it.
alternatives.B: I show a simple first version early to get real reactions quickly.

VOICE-04.prompt: A decision is taking shape in your team that you assess differently on professional grounds. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I make my professional objection clear before the decision is final in the team.
alternatives.B: I support the decision to keep the team able to act, and raise concerns during implementation.

EVI-05.prompt: Someone on the team sees something differently than you and raises a comprehensible point. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I first check the point against further evidence and keep my assessment until then.
alternatives.B: I go through the point right away and question my own assessment while doing so.

EXP-06.prompt: You have to make a decision for which some information is still missing. But you know the field very well. How strongly do you rely on your own experience when choosing?

VOICE-05.prompt: The group wants to close a topic, but one point is not quite settled for you. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I stop the closing and say openly that I am not there yet on this point.
alternatives.B: I allow the closing so that we make progress, and settle my point right after the meeting.

ORG-07.prompt: You are working in a focused way on an important topic and an equally important new request comes in. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I interrupt fairly quickly and take care of the new request right away.
alternatives.B: I first hold on to my current task and push the new one back.

EVI-06.prompt: Two reliable sources come to different assessments on a question. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I weigh which assessment fits our situation better and keep working with it.
alternatives.B: I look into the contradiction more closely to understand where the difference comes from.

ORG-08.prompt: Your plan basically still works, but several smaller things are going differently than expected. Which describes you better?

alternatives.A: I only change my plan when the deviations really start to matter.
alternatives.B: I prefer to adjust my plan continuously, even for smaller changes.
